note: Identity and requirement context of the repository-level architecture rules checked in CI. A rule id is local to this file. `requirements` names the requirements the rule protects, as worded in 01; `architecture` repeats their ALLOCATED_TO from 03 §17 (checked by ci/tests/test_architecture_rules.py); `exception_allowed` says whether ci/architecture/exceptions.json may carry a temporary, change-controlled exception for it. A rule that fails is reported with these fields. Adding a rule needs its checker, a negative test and an entry here (checked by ci/tests/test_architecture_rules.py).

rules.summary: Every contract declares one registered canonical producer, and contract ids are unique
rules.why_no_exception: Producer authority is the registry's integrity; a contract without one canonical producer has no authority to test against.

rules.summary: A service other than manufacturing-core does not import a database driver or ORM
A service other than manufacturing-core does not import manufacturing_core directly
Service source does not assign a literal credential
rules.why_no_exception: A committed secret is never made acceptable by a record; it is removed and rotated.

rules.summary: Architecture exceptions are well-formed, approved, unexpired, within the time limit and still needed
rules.why_no_exception: This is the exception process itself. It has no requirement of its own: it keeps the requirements of the excepted rule from being waived informally (01, Requirement Waivers).
